subject: Redline runbook: MSA + Order Form sequencing for Q3 renewal
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cascade.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baines <tom.baines@cascade.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cascade renewal — initial redline and sequencing question

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Attached is our annotated redline of the MSA with two asks that will affect sequencing:

1) We need a term shift to align the new 18-month committed term to the fiscal quarter boundary (starts 2027-07-01).
2) We want the new capacity to be additive (stacking) for the first full billing period rather than a pro-rata adjustment; our finance team prefers a clean billing cutover.

Our procurement team is sensitive to signature order. We typically require the Master Services Agreement to be fully executed before order forms are countersigned, but we can be flexible if Redwood provides a runbook showing step-by-step gating, rollback, and invoicing treatment. Can you send a runbook that spells out signature sequencing, who signs first, and how billing will be handled for the capacity uplift?

Attached: cascade_msa_redline_20270404.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

Requested timeline: procurement needs a DocuSign packet by 2027-04-10 to remain on track for the July start.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Procurement, Cascade Systems
procurement@cascade.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cascade.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cascade renewal — initial redline and sequencing question

Elena — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass "runbook" that outlines the suggested sequencing and roles. High-level proposal:

- Step 1 (Legal): Agree core MSA language (definitions, term, liability) and lock Exhibit A (scope) in redline form.
- Step 2 (Commercial/Legal): Finalize Order Form with capacity figures and pricing, mark as "pending execution" referencing the MSA effective date.
- Step 3 (Signatures): Option A ("preferred by Redwood") — countersign Order Form first, then execute MSA; Option B (procurement preference) — execute MSA first, then Order Form. The runbook describes controls for both.
- Step 4 (Billing): If cascade prefers stacking for the first billing period, Redwood will issue a one-time invoice for the delta on the first full period and mark it as non-prorated per mutual agreement.

I've looped in Kimberly and Karthik to confirm legal and ops feasibility. Can you confirm which signature order Cascade prefers (MSA-first vs OrderForm-first)? If you accept the runbook approach, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet and a short mutual action plan (MAP).

Attachment: runbook_v1.docx (DOCX, 6 pages)

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Elena / Logan — quick legal read-through and recommended adjustments to the runbook. Key points from Legal: 

- We can support either signature order, but to minimize operational risk we recommend MSA be fully agreed (signatures or signature-ready redline with explicit effective date language) before any billing change is processed. That avoids disputes about effective date.
- For the term shift to align to 2027-07-01, Legal suggests an explicit clause: "Term start date shall be the later of (i) execution date and (ii) 2027-07-01 for the 18-month committed period" — this preserves your requested boundary while keeping execution flexible.
- On stacking vs pro-rata: Redwood can accept stacking as a commercial concession if Cascade signs a one-time non-refundable capacity activation fee. We'll note that in the Order Form as "Activation Charge."
- Exhibit mapping: please confirm which exhibits are moving (Exhibit B: SLAs; Exhibit C: Data & Security). We should lock exhibits in the order: Exhibits -> MSA -> Order Form in terms of internal review precedence.

I've attached a short spreadsheet that maps redline sections to runbook steps and an initial clause redraft for the term boundary.

Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 2 sheets)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-05T15:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cascade renewal — initial redline and sequencing question

Looping in Operations perspective. Two operational items to confirm before we finalize sequence: 

1) Capacity cutover date — if we use 2027-07-01 as the billing start for the 18-month term and Cascade wants stacking, we need a 7-day window post-signature to provision the extra GPUs to avoid throttling. That provisioning window should be reflected in the runbook as "Provisioning SLA: T+7 calendar days".

2) Billing system constraints — Redwood's billing backend cannot retroactively mark an order as "non-prorated" after an invoice has finalized. To avoid a manual credit, we should capture the activation charge and billing preference in the order form as a single-line item and set the invoice date to the first full billing period. If Cascade prefers otherwise, Ops will need a signed ticket to process manual adjustments.

I've attached an orderform_sequence_matrix.csv that maps sign date to provisioning and invoice outcomes for the four possible sequencing variants. Please review and confirm which path you want.

Attachment: orderform_sequence_matrix.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Cascade's position after internal review: 

- Procurement preference: MSA executed before the Order Form is countersigned. That said, we'll accept an "MSA-executed-in-policy" approach if Redwood can provide the signed MSA PDF or a DocuSign envelope indicating completion prior to finalizing billing.
- We accept the Activation Charge as a non-refundable one-time fee to allow stacking for the first full billing period. Please list it as a separate line on the Order Form and confirm the invoice schedule.
- Provisioning SLA: T+7 days is acceptable. Please include a rollback plan (described in the runbook) if provisioning fails or capacity is delayed.

Next steps for Redwood: 1) Legal to produce a final MSA PDF with the term boundary clause Kimberly suggested, 2) Commercial to prepare Order Form with Activation Charge and the chosen sign order noted, 3) Ops to confirm provisioning runbook entry. If we can get a DocuSign packet by 2027-04-10 that reflects the MSA-first preference, procurement will route for signatures that week.

Attached: cascade_msa_redline_20270406_final.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

Elena Morales
